title: Dehydration signs in a newborn
summary: Young babies can dry out quickly when feeds are low. Know the early clues.
whatsNormal:
A well-hydrated newborn usually has:

• At least 6 wet diapers per day once milk is in (days 5–7)
• Pale yellow urine (not dark orange)
• Moist mouth and tears when crying (after the first weeks)
• A soft spot that is flat, not sunken
• Wakes for feeds and has alert periods

In hot weather or illness, babies may need extra attention to fluids, follow your clinician's advice.
watchFor: Fewer wet diapers than expected for your baby's age in days
Dark yellow or orange urine after day 4
Sunken soft spot (fontanelle) or dry lips and mouth
Very sleepy, hard to wake, or weak suck
callDoctorIf: No wet diaper for 12+ hours after day 3
Sunken eyes, no tears when crying, or limpness
Fever under 3 months with poor feeding
Vomiting everything or refusing all feeds, seek care promptly

sources.title: American Academy of Pediatrics (HealthyChildren.org): How to tell if baby is getting enough milk
